newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Arab lawmaker angry over security adviser.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Arab lawmaker angry over security adviser.

text.p: A former Israeli secret service agent who was quoted as saying he killed captured Palestinian hijackers now serves as a security adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a legislator said on Monday.
Azmi Bishara, an Israeli Arab member of parliament, said in a statement he had asked Netanyahu why he appointed someone who "boasted publicly of crushing Palestinian skulls".
Israel's biggest newspaper, Yedioth Ahronoth, quoted the adviser, Ehud Yatom, as saying last August that he killed two Palestinian hijackers who were captured after seizing an Israeli bus in 1984.

"We put them in our van and then I received instructions from (Shin Bet domestic security chief) Avraham Shalom to kill them, so I killed them with a big stone. I crushed their skulls," Yedioth quoted Yatom as saying.
The prime minister's office, under which the Shin Bet operates, denied at the time that Yatom made the comments. But the newspaper said it stood by its story.
Asked about Yatom's position, an official at Netanyahu's office said: "He is a member of a special council on counter-terrorism." The official did not elaborate.

After the killings, the Shin Bet mounted an elaborate coverup that led to the resignation of Shalom and three other top agency officials. They received presidential pardons along with seven other agents, including Yatom.
